questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I love Italy and have travelled there a lot since I have family there. Generally love the culture, the food, the weather.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. However, the information is provided quite late, but I felt like all the information needed was provided, but you should keep in mind that it will be provided late, but no later than you're expected to sign up for classes etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: You don't receive any assistance in person, but all the information I needed was provided via e-mail

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Information on the different types of exams could have been better for some of the classes.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I just found mine on Airbnb.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There's no big difference from living off campus in my home country. For your own sake it's easiest if you find housing near the metro lines going close by campus, but that's just for convenience.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't check the housing for students.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very easy, but the classes are quite small (3 or 6 ECTS) so it can be a bit difficult to make sure your classes don't overlap, but all the information needed to check schedules and sign up is easily provided.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
You sign up for classes on
unimia.unimi.it
. It's very easy, you just type in the name of the class, teacher, and number of ECTS.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Information was provided via e-mail. I didn't need any extra help so I can't say anything about that.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the steps in the e-mail, it's very easy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of different classes which was nice, but I don't think the academic programme was that challenging.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was definitely lower than at home. There's pretty much no at home studying, you just have to show up for the classes, and quite a few of the exams were just presentations in class.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different as there's more classes and much less studying on your own.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Law and policies of social rights protection in Europe
2. Comparative constitutional traditions 
3. Cultural diversity and Human Rights Law 
4. Law and economics of green transition and social justice
5. International Criminal Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them except green transition as that one was quite boring and it had a lot of economics and economic theories in it considering it's a law school class.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No unexpected cost. I kept my Danish phone number so I didn't spend anything extra on that. Personal covers both shopping and traveling

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't explores this.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: ESN provides lots of activities for exchange students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I only did ESN tours.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel a lot! Milan is located perfectly for traveling Italy and even Southern France and Northern Switzerland

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the Italians are friendly and easy-going.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didn't really do this.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: All of it!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Don't stress too much about the academic prospects.
2. Travel a lot.
3. Buy the museum card at novocento close to Duomo.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of information is provided very late on but don't stress about this as the deadlines are also very late and typically not that strict. I signed up for classes less than a weak before they started.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new friends from all over the world and traveling a lot.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: None really.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
